title: Local presentability of accessible many-sorted monad algebras
statement:
Fix a universe $\mathcal U$. A category is locally presentable if it has $\mathcal U$-small Hom sets, all $\mathcal U$-small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and, for some infinite regular cardinal $\kappa\in\mathcal U$, a $\mathcal U$-small family of $\kappa$-presentable objects generating every object under $\kappa$-filtered colimits. Here $\kappa$-filtered means every diagram with fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms has a cocone, and $\kappa$-presentable means its Hom functor preserves these colimits. Regular means a union of fewer than $\kappa$ sets of size less than $\kappa$ still has size less than $\kappa$.

Let $S$ be a $\mathcal U$-small set and let $\mathcal C_s$ be locally presentable categories. Their product $\mathcal C=\prod_{s\in S}\mathcal C_s$ is locally presentable. Let $T:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ be a functor with natural transformations $\eta:1\to T$ and $\mu:T^2\to T$ satisfying $\mu T\mu=\mu\mu T$ and $\mu T\eta=1=\mu\eta T$. Assume that $T$ preserves $\lambda$-filtered colimits for some infinite regular $\lambda\in\mathcal U$. The category of $T$-algebras is locally presentable, and hence complete and cocomplete. Its objects are pairs $(A,a)$ with $a:TA\to A$, $a\eta_A=1_A$ and $aT(a)=a\mu_A$; its morphisms $f:(A,a)\to(B,b)$ satisfy $fa=bT(f)$. Completeness and cocompleteness mean existence of every $\mathcal U$-small limit and colimit. No assertion that the algebra category has the same presentability cardinal as its base is made.

source.place: Agent-formulated general input to paragraph 2. WANTED: Adamek--Rosicky, Locally Presentable and Accessible Categories, Theorem 2.78 and closure under small products. Ching--Riehl, Coalgebraic models for combinatorial model categories, Appendix A, pp. 9-11, explicitly states the accessible-monad theorem after Proposition A.1 and explains accessible PIE limits. Read online at https://math.jhu.edu/~eriehl/coalgebraic.pdf; not archived. No Stacks tag states this presentability theorem.

external.place: Ching--Riehl, Appendix A, Proposition A.1 and the following paragraph (Adamek--Rosicky 2.78); Theorem A.2; Definition A.3 and closure under PIE limits, printed pp. 9-11. The product clause follows from accessibility of small products and their componentwise colimits.

proof.text: Each $\mathcal C_s$ is accessible by the definition of local presentability. Apply the small-product clause of [lem-coef-accessible-pie-closure] to obtain accessibility of $\mathcal C=\prod_s\mathcal C_s$. Its Hom sets are small: $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(X,Y)=\prod_s\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_s}(X_s,Y_s)$ is a small product of small sets.

source.place: Paragraph 2 categorical foundation; Ching--Riehl Appendix A, PIE-closure theorem before Definition A.3, product case.

proof.text: For a small diagram $D:J\to\mathcal C$, choose the colimit $L_s$ of each component diagram $D_s:J\to\mathcal C_s$. The component cocones assemble to a cocone $D\to(L_s)_s$. A cocone $D\to Y$ determines a unique map $L_s\to Y_s$ for each $s$, and these give the unique map $(L_s)_s\to Y$ factoring that cocone, by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Thus $\mathcal C$ is cocomplete. Along with Step 1 this is local presentability as defined in the statement, including the empty product.

source.place: Paragraph 2 categorical foundation; agent verification of the componentwise colimit universal property.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-accessible-completeness-characterization], the locally presentable category $\mathcal C$ is complete. Both $T$ and $1_{\mathcal C}$ are accessible: the first by the stated preservation hypothesis, the second because it preserves every existing colimit. Form $\mathcal I=\operatorname{Ins}(T,1_{\mathcal C})$. By [lem-coef-accessible-pie-closure], $\mathcal I$ and its forgetful projection $p:\mathcal I\to\mathcal C$ are accessible. Concretely an object is $(A,a:TA\to A)$, with no laws yet, and its morphisms satisfy exactly $fa=bT(f)$. There is a tautological natural transformation $\alpha:Tp\Rightarrow p$ with component $a$.

source.place: Paragraph 2 categorical foundation; Ching--Riehl Appendix A proof of Proposition A.1, first stage, with the inserter reversed for monads.

proof.text: On $\mathcal I$, the two transformations $\alpha\circ\eta_p$ and $1_p$ have the same accessible source and target functor $p$. Their components are $a\eta_A$ and $1_A$. They are natural since $fa=bT(f)$ and $T(f)\eta_A=\eta_Bf$ imply $fa\eta_A=b\eta_Bf$. Take their equifier $\mathcal E\hookrightarrow\mathcal I$. By [lem-coef-accessible-pie-closure], $\mathcal E$ and its inclusion are accessible. It is the full subcategory satisfying the unit law.

source.place: Paragraph 2 categorical foundation; Ching--Riehl Appendix A proof of Proposition A.1, second stage, with monad unit in place of comonad counit.

proof.text: Write $q:\mathcal E\to\mathcal C$ for the composite forgetful functor and again $\alpha:Tq\Rightarrow q$ for the restriction. Composites of the accessible functors occurring here are accessible: choose a regular cardinal at least as large as their finitely many preservation cardinals and the cardinals witnessing existence of filtered colimits in each intervening accessible category. A diagram filtered for this cardinal is filtered for each smaller one, so all its intermediate colimits exist and every functor preserves them. For two such functors $F,G$ and a colimit cocone $D\to L$, applying $F$ and then $G$ gives successive colimit cocones, hence $GF(L)$ with its induced cocone is the colimit of $GF(D)$. This proves accessibility of $q$ and $T^2q$. The transformations $\alpha\circ T\alpha$ and $\alpha\circ\mu_q:T^2q\Rightarrow q$ are natural. Explicitly $faT(a)=bT(f)T(a)=bT(fa)=bT(b)T^2(f)$, whereas $fa\mu_A=bT(f)\mu_A=b\mu_BT^2(f)$. Their equifier is accessible by [lem-coef-accessible-pie-closure]. Its objects satisfy exactly $a\eta_A=1_A$ and $aT(a)=a\mu_A$, and its arrows are exactly those of the given $T$-algebra category. Hence that category is accessible.

source.place: Paragraph 2 categorical foundation; Ching--Riehl Appendix A proof of Proposition A.1, third stage, with multiplication in place of comultiplication.

proof.text: Construct limits in the algebra category directly. For a small diagram $j\mapsto(A_j,a_j)$, use completeness from Step 3 to choose an underlying limit $(L,p_j)$ in $\mathcal C$. The maps $a_jT(p_j):TL\to A_j$ form a cone: for a diagram arrow $f:A_i\to A_j$, one has $fa_iT(p_i)=a_jT(f)T(p_i)=a_jT(p_j)$. There is therefore a unique $a:TL\to L$ with $p_ja=a_jT(p_j)$.

source.place: Paragraph 2 categorical foundation; agent calculation from the limit universal property and the displayed monad algebra identities. Structure map and cone compatibility.

proof.text:
For the structure map $a:TL\to L$ constructed in Step 6, verify the two algebra laws. The projections are jointly monic by their limit universal property. Naturality of $\eta$ gives $p_ja\eta_L=a_j\eta_{A_j}p_j=p_j$, so $a\eta_L=1_L$. Likewise
$$p_jaT(a)=a_jT(p_ja)=a_jT(a_j)T^2(p_j)=a_j\mu_{A_j}T^2(p_j)=a_jT(p_j)\mu_L=p_ja\mu_L,$$
so the associativity law holds.

source.place: Paragraph 2 categorical foundation; agent calculation from the limit universal property and the displayed monad algebra identities. Unit and multiplication laws, checked after limit projections.

proof.text: For the algebra $(L,a)$ from Steps 6-7, verify the limit universal property. For a cone of algebra maps $h_j:(B,b)\to(A_j,a_j)$, its unique underlying mediator $h:B\to L$ satisfies $p_jhb=h_jb=a_jT(h_j)=p_jaT(h)$; joint monicity gives $hb=aT(h)$. Thus this cone is a limit in the algebra category. The construction also works for the empty diagram: uniqueness of every map into the underlying terminal object gives all the required equalities. No preservation of limits by $T$ was used.

source.place: Paragraph 2 categorical foundation; agent calculation from the limit universal property and the displayed monad algebra identities. Algebra mediator and uniqueness, including the empty diagram.

proof.text: The algebra category has small Hom sets because each Hom set is a subset of a Hom set of $\mathcal C$, cut out by $fa=bT(f)$. It is accessible by Steps 3-5 and complete by Steps 6-8, so [lem-coef-accessible-completeness-characterization] implies that it is locally presentable and cocomplete as well. This proves every asserted existence of small limits and colimits. The accessibility theorem allows its cardinal to grow, so the argument imposes no equality between the base's and algebra category's presentability cardinals.
